questions.text:
2-chlorobutane exists as enantiomers (optical isomers).

CH₃–CH₂–CH–CH₃
                  |
                 Cl

Draw the enantiomers of 2-chlorobutane in the box below.
questions.expectedAnswer: Two 3D structural drawings showing the four different groups (CH₃, C₂H₅, H, Cl) arranged...
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Recognises tetrahedral arrangement of atoms/groups about asymmetric C atom. AND identifies the asymmetric (chiral) C atom.

questions.text: Explain why 2-chlorobutane can exist as enantiomers.
questions.expectedAnswer: 2-chlorobutane can exist as enantiomers because it is chiral
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies the asymmetric C atom. Merit: Draws TWO correct 3D structures of 2-chlorobutane AND explains the requirement for enantiomers.

questions.text:
Devise a reaction scheme to convert 2-chlorobutane into butanamide.

CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–C(=O)–NH₂   (butanamide)

For each step include:
• the reagents
• the structural formula of the organic product after each step.
questions.expectedAnswer: Step 1: 2-chlorobutane + KOH(alc)/heat → but-1-ene (elimination).
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: ONE correct conversion with reagent. Merit: THREE correct conversions with reagents. Excellence: Devised a complete reaction scheme.

questions.text:
Polylactic acid (PLA) is a polyester with various uses, including medical implants, tissue engineering, and 3D printing. It is made from lactic acid, shown below:

HO–CH–C(=O)–OH
       |
      CH₃

In the box below, draw a section of the PLA chain to show THREE repeating units.
questions.expectedAnswer: Three repeating units showing: –[O–CH(CH₃)–C(=O)]₃– with ester linkages (–COO–) formed between...
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Draws polymer with ester linkages. Merit: Correctly draws THREE repeating units.

questions.text: Identify and explain the type of reaction occurring to form PLA.
questions.expectedAnswer: Condensation (polymerisation) reaction
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies condensation (polymerisation). Merit: Explains condensation (polymerisation) — ester bond formed with loss of water.

questions.text:
Below is the structural formula of a dipeptide:

H₂N–C(H)(CH₃)–C(=O)–N(H)–C(H)(CH₂COOH)–COOH

Circle the amide (peptide) linkage on the dipeptide above.
questions.expectedAnswer: Circle the –C(=O)–N(H)– group (the amide/peptide bond) linking the two amino acid residues.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correctly circles amide (peptide) linkage.

questions.text:
The dipeptide can undergo a chemical reaction to form the following products:

⁺H₃N–CH(CH₃)–COO⁻    and    ⁺H₃N–CH(CH₂COOH)–COO⁻

Identify and justify the type of chemical reaction that has occurred to form the above products.
questions.expectedAnswer: Acidic hydrolysis has occurred. Water has been used to split/break the amide (peptide) linkage
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Recognises that the amide/peptide linkage has been broken by water (hydrolysis reaction). Merit: Explains the process of acidic hydrolysis and gives one correct structural formula for either amino acid.

questions.text: Draw the structural formulae of the organic products formed when the dipeptide is heated under reflux with sodium hydroxide solution.
questions.expectedAnswer: Two products: H₂N–CH(CH₃)–COO⁻Na⁺ (sodium alaninate) and H₂N–CH(CH₂COO⁻Na⁺)–COO⁻Na⁺ (sodium...
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Draws two organic products (accept COO⁻/COONa). Merit: Draws correct structural formulae showing –COO⁻ instead of –COOH.

questions.text:
Complete the table below to show the structural formula or the IUPAC (systematic) name for each compound.

Compound A: IUPAC name = methyl propanoate
Compound B: structural formula = CH₃–CH₂–C(=O)–CH₂–CH₃
Compound C: structural formula = CH₃–CH₂–C(=O)(Cl)–H (with Cl on the C next to the carbonyl)
Compound D: IUPAC name = 2-hydroxybutanoyl chloride
questions.expectedAnswer: A: CH₃–O–C(=O)–CH₂–CH₃ (methyl propanoate is an ester).
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: THREE correct from part (a)(i). Merit: ALL correct for part (a).

questions.text: Draw THREE constitutional (structural) isomers of Compound C that contain a carbonyl group (C=O).
questions.expectedAnswer: Three structural isomers of C₃H₅ClO containing a carbonyl group.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: TWO correct from part (a)(ii). Merit: ALL correct.

questions.text:
Complete the flowchart below by drawing the structural formulae for Compounds A, B, C, D, and E, and identifying Reagents 1, 2, 3, and 4.

Starting material: propan-2-ol (CH₃–CH(OH)–CH₃)
→ conc. H₂SO₄, heat → Compound A
Compound A + H₂O/H⁺ → Compound B
Compound A + Reagent 2 → Compound D
Compound D + Reagent 3 → CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–NH₂
CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–NH₂ + H₂SO₄(aq) → Compound E
Compound B + Reagent 1 → Compound C
Compound C + Compound E + Reagent 4 → CH₃–CH₂–C(=O)–H–N(CH₂CH₂CH₃)
questions.expectedAnswer: Compound A: CH₃–CH=CH₂ (propene, via elimination/dehydration).
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: FIVE correct entries. Merit: SEVEN correct. Excellence: ALL compounds and reagents correct.

questions.text:
The following table lists the structural formulae for six different organic compounds.

1: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂OH
2: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–C(=O)H
3: CH₃=CH–CH₂–C(=O)H
4: CH₃–CH=CH–C(=O)(Cl)
5: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–C(=O)(Cl)
6: CH₃=CH–C(=O)–CH₃

Choose the appropriate organic compounds from the table above to match the observations recorded from chemical tests. Enter the chosen compound number in the table below.

• Heating with acidified potassium dichromate, K₂Cr₂O₇(aq)/H⁺, causes the solution to change from orange to green. Heating with Tollens' reagent does not produce a silver mirror.
• Heating with Fehling's reagent forms an orange-red solid. Mixing with potassium permanganate solution, KMnO₄(aq), causes the purple solution to decolourise and a brown solid to form.
• Mixing with bromine water, Br₂(aq), results in steamy fumes, and the solution changes from orange to colourless.
questions.expectedAnswer: Test 1 (dichromate goes green, Tollens' negative): Compound 1 (primary alcohol
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Select THREE correct compounds. Merit: Links FOUR observations to functional groups and identifies at least THREE reaction types. Excellence: Links ALL observations to functional groups/compounds with correct reaction types.

questions.text:
Justify your chosen structural formula for each of the three compounds.

Your answer should:
• relate the observations to the functional groups identified
• identify and explain the types of reactions involved.
questions.expectedAnswer: Compound 1: Primary alcohol (–CH₂OH) is oxidised by acidified dichromate (orange→green = Cr₂O₇²⁻...
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Recognises at least THREE types of reactions. Merit: Links FOUR observations to functional groups and identifies THREE reaction types. Excellence: Links ALL observations to the TWO compounds, identifying reaction types for third compound with reference to all properties provided.

questions.text:
A student followed the procedure outlined below to prepare a pure sample of ethyl propanoate in the laboratory:

Step 1: Add propanoic acid, ethanol, and concentrated H₂SO₄ to a round-bottomed flask.
Step 2: Heat the reaction mixture under reflux for 30 minutes.
Step 3: Add sodium carbonate until the bubbling stops.
Step 4: Add water and separate the layers.
Step 5: Add a drying agent to the organic layer.
Step 6: Distill the organic layer to purify the ethyl propanoate.

Describe the function of the concentrated H₂SO₄ added in step 1.
questions.expectedAnswer: The concentrated H₂SO₄ acts as a dehydrating agent to remove water
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies the role of H₂SO₄ as catalyst/dehydrating agent.

questions.text:
Give TWO reasons to explain why the reaction mixture was heated under reflux in step 2.

(1)
(2)
questions.expectedAnswer: (1) Heating increases the rate of reaction by providing more energy to reactant particles /...
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Recognises ONE reason. Merit: Recognises TWO reasons for heating under reflux.

questions.text: Why was sodium carbonate added in step 3?
questions.expectedAnswer: The sodium carbonate neutralises the concentrated H₂SO₄ and any remaining propanoic acid...
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies that sodium carbonate neutralises the acid(s).

questions.text:
Explain how distillation was used in step 6 to purify the ethyl propanoate from the organic layer.

Your answer should refer to relevant boiling point(s) from the table below.

Propanoic acid: 141 °C
Ethanol: 78.3 °C
Ethyl propanoate: 99.1 °C
questions.expectedAnswer: The reaction mixture is heated to approximately 97–101 °C to purify the ethyl propanoate.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Recognises that the boiling point determines which substance distils first. Merit: Explains how distillation is used to purify by referencing boiling points. Excellence: Justifies how distillation separates all substances with reference to their boiling points and the collection temperature.

questions.text:
Consider Compounds A, B, and C, shown below:

Compound A: CH₃–CH₂–C(=O)(Cl)–H (2-chloropropanal-like)
Compound B: CH₃–CH(OH)–CH₂–NH₂
Compound C: CH₃–C(=O)(CH₂)(NH₂)–H

Choose the ONE compound that has ALL the following properties:
• cannot exist as enantiomers (optical isomers)
• forms a silver mirror when heated with Tollens' reagent
• turns damp red litmus paper blue.

Compound (A, B, or C): ___

Explain your choice.
questions.expectedAnswer: Compound C. Compound C does not have an asymmetric carbon atom, so it cannot exist as enantiomers
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Chooses Compound C. Merit: Explains choice of Compound C in terms of at least TWO properties.

questions.text:
Draw the structural formula for the constitutional (structural) isomer of C₃H₅OCl that has the following properties:
• exists as enantiomers (optical isomers)
• branched carbon chain
• produces steamy fumes upon addition of water.
questions.expectedAnswer: CH₃–CH(Cl)–C(=O)–H... or more likely a branched acyl chloride/structure with an asymmetric carbon
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Draws a branched chain / acyl chloride group / asymmetric C atom. Merit: Draws correct structural formula.

questions.text:
Draw the structural formula for the constitutional (structural) isomer of C₄H₇OBr that has the following properties:
• exists as cis-trans (geometric) isomers
• straight chain arrangement
• causes a colour change of orange to green when heated with acidified potassium dichromate to produce an organic product that does not react with Benedict's solution.
questions.expectedAnswer: The compound must have a C=C double bond (for cis-trans isomers), a straight chain, and a...
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Draws a C=C double bond / secondary alcohol group. Merit: Draws correct structural formula for either (ii) OR (iii). Excellence: Draws correct structural formulae for (ii) AND (iii), AND explains choice of Compound C with reference to all properties provided.
